- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., recent sentiment change > 0.5) and model overestimates, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment turns negative or stabilizes after a spike, model should adjust downward — especially if true outcome shows mean reversion or pullback.
- Model tends to overpredict in early days of high sentiment volatility — apply a 5–10% downward bias for 3–5 day horizons following sentiment spikes.
- When news volume is low (0.0) and sentiment is neutral or declining, model should not overreact — avoid sharp upward revisions.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, check for sentiment lag — adjust downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment history shows strong upward trend but model is flat or slightly downward, increase forecast by 2–5% to capture momentum.
- If sentiment change is negative and model is still rising, apply a “sentiment correction” — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes or reverses.
